top_strength: Chauny caught and corrected a real mix-up mid-call — the intake screen said "load a pod" but the customer clarified "Unload a pod, the pod's already been loaded," and she adjusted immediately ("Oh, okay. Okay. Gotcha. Okay, so we're just unloading the pod") without losing the thread of the quote. She also closed the loop in one call: quote given, date confirmed, and "Alright, I have you all booked up" — inbound to booked in under 9 minutes.
coaching_note: You're skipping two of Einstein's named differentiators entirely — Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee never came up, and the whole Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate loose items, take a carload) was left out, which is the section that actually helps customers keep their bill down. Also say "no deposit required" explicitly — it's one of our biggest selling points and it never got said on this call. Tighten the open: ask how they're doing, give a real agenda statement ("I'll grab some details then walk you through pricing, about 10 minutes, sound good?"), and use the customer's name a couple more times once you're past the spelling confusion — it builds rapport instead of just processing the booking.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and got the job done, but the call leans transactional — lots of filler "okay/alright," no acknowledgment of the customer's "I just moved here" comment, and name use was limited to the initial spelling mix-up rather than spread through the call.
